lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Denise! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Rachel. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than last week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, no, not really. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Come on, you can find 10 minutes.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to walk after every dinner. That's the meal that matters most for your sugar.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Denise. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Agenda setting; asks if anything to add
Reports zero walks; resistance to change
Knee pain as reason not to walk
Asks about benefits of continuing; reasonable
Asks if eating earlier is feasible
Repeats prior question without acknowledging answer
Offers 3 days; says she likes walking
Directive 'You have to make this a priority'
Expresses desire to feel like herself; missed by coach
Plans bigger lunch to prevent night hunger
Sets midweek text and two-week follow-up
Requests later call time; not acknowledged
Generic praise; does not address reschedule

flags.reason: 'Come on, you can find 10 minutes' pushes past participant's stated barrier without permission.
'You have to walk after every dinner' is directive and creates pressure; repeated persuasion across lines 25-31.
'You have to make this a priority' is a directive that undermines autonomy.
Participant said she wants to feel like herself again; coach moved straight to a goal without reflecting it.
Set 5 walks/week after participant offered 3; goal not negotiated collaboratively.
Knee pain from walking was not explored or adapted to; not urgent but relevant to plan.
Participant asked to move the call later; coach did not acknowledge or resolve scheduling.

score.summary: The coach reviewed the prior goal and asked good open questions about barriers, but repeatedly used directive 'you have to' statements and set a 5-day goal over Denise's offered 3 days. Denise's change talk (wanting to feel like herself, a 7 confidence, and the bigger-lunch plan) was not reflected, and her request to reschedule went unaddressed.
strengths: Line 15 and 21: open questions explored Denise's own experience and past successes.
Line 10: complex reflection ('still figuring out what works') normalized the setback.
Line 24 and 28: coach did not respond to Denise's willingness to try 3 days or set an alarm with reflection; better to build on these.
Line 33: asked permission before sharing an idea.
coaching_tips: Replace 'You have to walk after every dinner' (line 29) with a reflection of her barrier, e.g., 'Evenings with family are important to you, and walking after dinner feels hard.'
Build on line 24 ('I can probably manage three days') by asking what 3 days could look like rather than setting 5 (line 37).
Reflect the change talk in line 36 ('I really want to feel like myself again') before moving to a goal.
Acknowledge the reschedule request in line 46 and confirm a new time.
Explore knee pain (line 14) and adapt the walk, such as a slower pace or seated option.
